gown.textures: ue5/tools/textures/garment.py -> C:/TownChess/assets/garment/T_PatientGown_{Shirt,Short}_{BC,ARM}.png (workspace only: painted on the Epic DefaultGarment AO/stitch masks, exported by an editor step to C:/TownChess/assets/garment_src). Canvas linear 0.17/0.155/0.12 mottled; dirt pooled in the folds (AO) + film + blotches; soiled frayed seams/hems (stitch mask, island edges); collar ring; 10 sweat areas with tide lines; 24 dried-blood stains (dark brown-red, darker rims, soaked halo) + 4 big ones on the front chest, spatter, drips; 9 rust smears; roughness 0.9 canvas, 0.62 blood, damp sweat lower
gown.material: outfit_slot_material -> gown_material(): M_TC_PBR instance per garment slot of MI_PatientShirt (patient and player body): BaseColor/ARM ours, Normal = the garment's own DG_*_Normal (folds and seams kept), DetailNormal = rough_linen weave tiling 14 faded by DetailFadeInv 20 (no sub-pixel weave at the seat), two-sided override. TC_GARMENT_DIR, default C:/TownChess/assets/garment; without the PNGs the C3 colour-only child is used
gown.jacket: MI_PatientJacket: grime threshold 0.3 -> 0.12, darker grime colour, new master NormalFadeInv 20 (C7-gown.jpg dither)
gown.face: patient_face_materials(): children of the face's baked skin MIs (the component holds MIDs; parent resolved by name; a child of the MID rendered as clay in the first build) with Roughness Global Multiply x0.82 and Specular Global Multiply x0.9 (damp sheen). The Basecolor Value/Saturation post-bake controls are not factors (0.88 rendered the skin saturated red) and are not used
gown.evidence: C8m-opponent.jpg: opponent vs run 6, gown close-up vs m8b, the gown in the base-colour buffer after. At the seat the visible upper chest still reads light; the heavy stains sit lower on the gown

skin.srmf: skin.py --srmf T_Body_SRMF_VT.tga (8K; R specular, G roughness, B 0, A mask) writes T_PlayerSkin_<var>_SRMF.png: roughness +0.4 crease dirt (at least 'dirty' strength), +0.12 film, +0.3 nail dirt, +-0.08 slow drift, +0.06 palms, -0.15 nail plates; dirty variant (patient) damp, -0.15 off the dirt; specular x0.82 x(1 - 0.5 dirt - ...) x(1 + 0.3 nails)
skin.import: player_skins(): BC and SRMF imported under versioned names (_C8): picked up once without TC_SKIN_REIMPORT, older revisions keep theirs; SRMF compression/sRGB copied from the parent's T_Body_SRMF_VT (TC_MASKS, linear); MI_PlayerSkin_* recreated every build; Specular Global Multiply x0.75 on the parent's value. Skin PNGs are Epic-derived, workspace only: C:/TownChess/assets/skin_c8 via TC_SKIN_DIR until accepted (C:/TownChess/assets/skin untouched; copy BC+SRMF there or set TC_SKIN_DIR to adopt)
skin.evidence: C8m-hands.jpg (vs run 6). Modest: less uniform highlight, redder knuckles, paler palms; still tan-orange at the seat

sleeve: sleeve.py: wear-mask B = weave fade on the rolled cuff (master: NormalStrength x (1 - WearMask.B)); a wider, darker elbow gather. The 'hard vertical edge' is where the C5 sleeve mesh ends in the body's shirt sleeve (props.py geometry, hands/character): open

wood.gouges: stains.py scratch(): each gouge one polygon with a smoothly varying width (no per-segment random rim), a thin continuous pale rim, lit and shaded groove walls; hairlines 260 pale-cored -> 150 mostly dark, a faint pale edge on a third. The 'chalk' strokes (main x 270-350) were those hairlines' pale rims
wood.board_dots: board.py: the grid was the normal-map pits (density 0.0012, one size: ~300 identical 0.2 mm craters per square); now 1/8 as many, clustered in the grime, three sizes, elongated along the grain, varied depth, dirt in them; fine dark specks 0.0009 -> 0.0004, clustered
wood.decals: M_TC_Blood slope fade: opacity x smoothstep(0.6, 0.85, |n.z|), n from ddx/ddy of the world position: no wear decal smears down a vertical face (complements C8b's placements)
wood.table: wood_table_worn MI: handling detail layer (DetailTiling 5, normal 0.5, rough 0.25, darken 0.12)
wood.evidence: C8m-wood.jpg. The gouges read as pale-outlined cuts; worth a judge look

rooks: master top mask (TopMaskZ/TopDarken/TopRough: up-facing surfaces above a mesh-local z, LocalPosition + VertexNormalWS); MI_RookWhiteCrown/BlackCrown on the rooks (top 1.4 cm of the 7.79 cm rook; darken 0.45/0.2, roughness +0.35). The crown reads darker and more even in close-ups; not measured against the specks at the seat FOV
